qt: to the Commission Marcin Sypniewski (ESN) Subject:

In view of the expiry at the end of 2028 of the derogation allowing high-emission units to participate in the Polish capacity market and the possibility of delays in bringing new generation capacity online, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Should the shortage of dispatchable capacity post 2028 be confirmed, does the current EU law provide for any other mechanisms to remunerate the availability of existing units in breach of the emission limits set in Article 22(4) of Regulation (EU) 2019/943, aside from the standard capacity market? If so, on what legal basis?

Given that current resource adequacy analyses show that replacement capacity will not be delivered on time, is the Commission considering introducing legislative changes to enable the support for such units to remain in place temporarily?

In light of the findings of the ENTSO-E European resource adequacy assessment, has the Commission examined the cross-border implications of a possible long-term dispatchable capacity shortage or major systemic failure in Poland post 2028, particularly the impact on the security of energy supply in neighbouring countries? If so, what are the results of that analysis, and what risk mitigation measures are planned?
